signal: Merger with Gallagher & Kennedy takes effect Dec. 1, creating a firm of 800+ lawyers and legal professionals, nearly 300 in Phoenix.
why_icp: Two firms, two sets of billing habits, one firm in six days. The first month after a merger is when unrecorded time and messy entries pile up.
first_line: With G&K joining on Dec. 1, you are about to have two ways of keeping time under one roof.

signal: Brought on a 40-lawyer team from Weil, including its would-be leader.
why_icp: A whole group arriving at once has to get onto new matter numbers and billing rules fast, and every missed hour in that switch is lost revenue.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Financial Officer or Director of Practice Management
first_line: Onboarding a 40-lawyer team in one go is a big timekeeping switch for everyone involved.

signal: Picked up Cahill partners as law firm churn continues after the Weil wind-down.
why_icp: Lateral partners bring clients mid-matter. Getting their time captured cleanly from day one protects the revenue that moved with them.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Financial Officer or Global Director of Finance Operations
first_line: Saw the Cahill partners joining. New laterals usually bring live matters, and those first weeks are where time slips.

signal: Launching a Silicon Valley office with Sullivan & Cromwell dealmakers.
why_icp: A new office built from laterals starts with no shared habits. Best time to set how time gets recorded is before the first big deal closes.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Operating Officer or Head of Finance
first_line: A new Silicon Valley office built from S&C dealmakers is a clean slate for how time gets recorded.

signal: Launching a Seattle office, the latest major firm to open there.
why_icp: New office, new hires, new local clients. Partners will want early numbers on how the office is doing, and that starts with clean time data.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Financial Officer or Director of Finance
first_line: Congrats on the Seattle launch. Early time data is usually how a new office proves itself.

signal: Expanding to South Florida through a merger with a boutique firm.
why_icp: Folding a boutique into an Am Law 100 firm means new timekeepers learning a bigger firm's billing guidelines, which is exactly where entries get kicked back.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Financial Officer or Director of Billing
first_line: Saw the South Florida merger. Boutique lawyers moving to bigger-firm billing rules is usually where time entries get rejected.

signal: Hired a 14-attorney aviation trial team from Cunningham Swaim to open a Dallas office.
why_icp: A trial boutique joining a global firm switches its whole team to new systems at once. Trial work is long and messy to reconstruct after the fact.
suggested_contact_title: US Chief Operating Officer or Finance Director
first_line: Congrats on the new Dallas office. Moving a 14-attorney trial team onto new systems is a lot of time to keep straight.

signal: Opening a Boston office with three IP partners from Lando & Anastasi; at least 18 people when it opens in the spring.
why_icp: IP partners and patent agents moving firms mid-matter, plus a new office to set up. Mid-size firm, so a pilot can move quickly.
suggested_contact_title: Managing Partner or Chief Financial Officer
first_line: Saw the Boston office news. Bringing over a whole IP group with patent agents is a good moment to fix how time gets captured.

signal: Opening a Cape May County office on the Jersey Shore, growing without a merger.
why_icp: South Jersey's largest firm growing office by office. A mid-size firm like this feels every unbilled hour, and can decide fast.
first_line: Congrats on the Cape May County office. Growing without a merger means every lawyer's billable hours carry more weight.

signal: Entered Virginia with its largest merger to date.
why_icp: A growth-by-merger firm adding a new state. Each merger brings another group of timekeepers onto the firm's systems.
suggested_contact_title: Chief Operating Officer or Director of Finance
first_line: Saw Gravis is now in Virginia. Each merger adds people who have to learn a new way to record time.
